label: Synesthetic thinking
summary: Synesthetic thinking, as Maaike uses the term, refers to a way of connecting dots between seemingly disparate topics. It describes a cognitive style that can look like aimless topic-hopping from the outside but functions as a strength in consultancy work. Maaike identifies it as something that sits uncomfortably inside rigid corporate structures but fits naturally with freelance work.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames synesthetic thinking as a personal trait she carried throughout her 20-year corporate career, where managers read it as a lack of consistent direction. Only after moving into freelance work did she reframe it as a superpower: the ability to draw connections across domains is exactly what makes her useful as a consultant. She does not theorise the concept in the abstract but uses it as a retrospective explanation for why corporate life never quite fit.
open_questions: Maaike names synesthetic thinking as a superpower in consulting but does not yet unpack how it concretely shows up in her conversation design or community building practice.
The passage gestures at the personal cost of suppressing this thinking style for 20 years in corporate life, but that thread is not fully explored.
